key_insight: Scientific ideas are not isolated inventions—they evolve through lineage, inheriting mechanisms, fixing weaknesses, and recombining prior work. This paper introduces a benchmark that tests whether AI can reason about those lineages and generate new ideas grounded in them.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks largely miss the structured inheritance behind scientific innovation, so they do not reveal whether AI systems can trace how ideas develop over time or use that history to propose credible next-step research ideas.
method: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a benchmark for scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation.
Organizes papers/proposals using the IdeaGene framework, representing each as a set of minimal inherited components rather than as isolated documents.
Evaluates whether models can identify ancestral relationships, track mechanism reuse and modification, and generate new ideas consistent with the observed lineage.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more realistic way to evaluate research assistants and idea-generation systems on scientific understanding rather than surface-level text matching. It can help build models that produce more credible, traceable, and innovation-aware research suggestions.
visual_elements: A lineage tree or genome-style branching diagram showing how ideas inherit and mutate across papers.
A benchmark pipeline graphic: source papers -> lineage decomposition -> reasoning tasks -> idea generation tasks.
Side-by-side comparison of "blank-slate idea generation" vs "lineage-grounded idea generation."
Icons for inheritance, mutation, recombination, and evaluation metrics.
paper_title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
paper_authors: Yifan Zhou, Qihao Yang, Yan Li, Donggang Li, Xiru Hu
